_README: Hand-reviewed exceptions to the athletes catalogue's mechanical rule
(scripts/build-catalog.mjs athletes — the artists' D266/D267 shape,
one domain over). NOT seeded to Firestore and not a question bank —
build input only, listed in check-content.mjs's NOT_SEEDED.
The rule keeps anyone at least a third of whose Wikidata occupations
are athletic (the P279* closure under Q2066131). Like the artists'
rule it does not finish, and in the same direction: P106 records
what a person DID, never what they are KNOWN FOR, and the list grows
with fame — so the raw rule dropped Serena Williams (2 of 7,
actor/writer/businessperson beside tennis) and Pelé (2 of 7,
actor/composer/politician beside football), while keeping Ursula
von der Leyen (1 of 3: physician, politician, equestrian).
HOW TO FILL IT. `node scripts/build-catalog.mjs athletes
--review-list 200` prints the ranked candidates with the fraction
that decided each. Then:
reject — in the catalogue, famous for something else. Needs `why`.
admit  — famous FOR sport, dropped by the ratio. No reason needed;
the name is the reason.
Every qid must be one the generator itself produced — applyReview()
can only drop a row or restore one from the candidate pool, never
mint a key — and the builder fails loudly on an entry whose subject
left the pool. check:catalogs holds both sides against the committed
catalogue. Keys are Wikidata QID numeric parts: 11459 means Q11459.

reject.name: Ursula von der Leyen
reject.why: Famous as a politician and Commission president; the equestrian occupation is biography, not the fame.
